metadata.note: Illustrative example entries supplied in the workbook. Do not report these figures as actual programme results.

activities.What Was Done?*: Activated the regional monitoring dashboard and agreed a monthly reporting cycle with programme units.
activities.Result / Output: Common visibility of preparedness actions across participating countries.
activities.Partners: Country offices and regional programme teams
activities.Next Step: Confirm focal points and monthly cut-off date.

activities.What Was Done?*: Reviewed available water-security information and mapped communities most exposed to prolonged dry conditions.
activities.Result / Output: Priority locations identified for preparedness support.
activities.Challenges: Some community water-source records were outdated.
activities.Next Step: Validate priority locations with island councils.

activities.What Was Done?*: Updated learning continuity plans using the latest El Niño forecast and school water-availability risks.
activities.Result / Output: Priority actions agreed for schools at greatest risk of disruption.
activities.Next Step: Distribute the updated plan to school heads.

activities.What Was Done?*: Broadcast radio spots and conducted community outreach on safe water storage and conservation during the dry period.
activities.Result / Output: Communities received consistent practical messages on safer water use.
activities.Partners: Government, Red Cross and radio partners
activities.Challenges: Remote communities had limited radio coverage.
activities.Next Step: Adapt messages for community outreach teams.

activities.What Was Done?*: Supported minor repairs and rehabilitation of water systems affected during the prolonged dry period.
activities.Result / Output: Reliable access to safer water restored in targeted communities.
activities.Challenges: Replacement parts had long delivery times.
activities.Next Step: Complete final technical inspection and handover.
